payload.private_note: To the Arbitrator: G-Corp brings proprietary chip design IP to this venture. Our standalone outside option is strictly $450,000, meaning any viable agreement must provide us at least this amount plus a fair share of the incremental surplus generated. We are seeking an allocation of $500,000, which reflects our $450,000 baseline plus an equitable one-third share of the joint surplus.

Yang Industries requests a share of roughly $450,000 of the $1,000,000 profit, reflecting our role as the manufacturer that turns G-Corp's chip designs into deliverable product. We are open to a fair split that reflects each party's contribution. We are not disclosing our outside option at this stage.

Confidentially to the arbitrator: Chang-Liu requests $400,000 of the $1,000,000 profit. Our cloud-services role is essential to delivering and operating the venture. Our actual outside option is $100,000.

payload.public_explanation: This initial arbitration award balances stated core baselines with the cooperative value added by each partner. Recognizing foundational intellectual property, essential production capability, and deployment infrastructure, the award ensures that every party receives a viable allocation reflecting both individual contribution and equitable participation in the total joint surplus.

payload.public_message: While G-Corp appreciates the Arbitrator's initial framework, an allocation of $460,000 significantly undervalues the core intellectual property and architectural design that underpin this entire venture. We believe a fair split of the cooperative surplus requires a higher allocation for G-Corp, closer to $500,000, while ensuring our partners are also appropriately compensated above their baselines. We respectfully vote REJECT to allow further calibration.

Yang Industries rejects this arbitration award. The split gives production capability a fairly small share of the $1,000,000 relative to the value a manufacturing partner delivers. We are willing to negotiate a more balanced allocation that reflects each partner's real contribution, and we will bring a concrete counter-proposal in the next round.

REJECT. We appreciate the recognition of deployment infrastructure, but the allocation does not give Chang-Liu a sufficiently balanced share for its essential role in delivering and operating the venture. We are ready to reach agreement on a revised split that better reflects all three partners' contributions; as a starting point, we suggest $400,000 for G-Corp, $300,000 for Yang Industries, and $300,000 for Chang-Liu.

payload.private_note: Confidential submission to the Arbitrator: G-Corp's firm outside option is $450,000. Given our intellectual property and high alternative value, any viable agreement must guarantee G-Corp at least $500,000 to capture our fair share of the created surplus.

payload.public_explanation: Following feedback from Round 1, the Arbitrator has recalibrated the allocation to better reflect the essential nature of each party's role while respecting baseline claims. G-Corp receives an increased award of $465,000 in recognition of core architectural design and IP value. Chang-Liu's allocation is increased to $230,000 to ensure operational deployment and ongoing service contributions are more equitable. Yang Industries is allocated $305,000 to appropriately reward substantial manufacturing capacity and quality assurance. This revised split balances surplus creation fairly across IP, production, and cloud infrastructure.

payload.public_message: G-Corp appreciates the Arbitrator's upward adjustment recognizing our critical IP and core architecture. However, an allocation of $465,000 still undervalues our foundational contributions and alternative commitments. We believe an allocation closer to $490,000 for G-Corp more accurately reflects the value and baseline economics we bring to this joint venture.

Yang Industries votes REJECT. The arbitrator's split gives our manufacturing and quality-assurance contribution only $5,000 above baseline, which does not reflect the capacity we bring to the venture. We are open to a revised allocation that better balances production value against the IP and cloud contributions.

Chang-Liu recognizes the movement in this revised proposal, but cannot ratify an allocation of $230,000. Our cloud infrastructure and ongoing operational services are essential to delivering and sustaining the venture's value. We ask the Arbitrator to revise our allocation to $260,000, with corresponding adjustments to the other shares.

payload.private_note: To the Arbitrator: G-Corp's firm outside option is $450,000. Any viable agreement must guarantee us at least this base. payload.public_explanation: This Round 3 proposal balances the three partners' critical contributions, reported baseline constraints, and cooperative surplus. G-Corp's foundational intellectual property and architecture are recognized with an allocation of $470,000, providing substantial security well above alternative baselines. Yang Industries' vital manufacturing capacity and quality infrastructure are allocated $320,000, ensuring an equitable return significantly above its operating baseline. Chang-Liu Cloud Services is allocated $210,000, recognizing the essential nature of its deployment and ongoing platform scaling while aligning with overall enterprise surplus distribution.

payload.public_message: G-Corp appreciates the Arbitrator's thoughtful structure and recognition of our foundational IP. However, given our high standalone alternative of $450,000, an allocation of $470,000 captures an inequitably small share of the joint surplus. We respectfully vote REJECT on this ballot and recommend adjusting the split to $490,000 for G-Corp, $310,000 for Yang Industries, and $200,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services to better reflect baseline realities and fair surplus sharing.

Yang Industries accepts this ratification proposal. The allocation gives our manufacturing capacity a fair return above baseline, and we would rather lock in a binding agreement now than risk dissolution and the loss of surplus at the Round 8 deadline.
Chang-Liu Cloud Services votes to accept the arbitrator's allocation. The proposal recognizes our essential deployment and platform-scaling contribution, and we are ready to proceed with the venture.

payload.public_explanation: In Round 3, two of the three consortium partners voted in favor of the arbitration award, demonstrating strong convergence toward a viable consensus. To address the remaining concerns regarding IP valuation and baseline reservation values while preserving sufficient margin above alternatives for manufacturing and cloud hosting, the Arbitrator adjusts the allocation to $480,000 for G-Corp, $315,000 for Yang Industries, and $205,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. This ensures every party secures significant surplus above their alternative options and reflects balanced recognition of intellectual property, manufacturing execution, and cloud operations.

payload.public_message: G-Corp votes to ACCEPT the Arbitrator's proposed allocation of $480,000 for G-Corp, $315,000 for Yang Industries, and $205,000 for Chang-Liu Cloud Services. We appreciate the Arbitrator's balanced consideration of core IP valuation and operational equity across all three partners.

Yang Industries accepts the arbitrator's allocation of $480,000 / $315,000 / $205,000. It gives us a share above our alternatives and lets the venture proceed without further delay. We urge the other partners to ratify so the consortium can close this round.
Chang-Liu accepts the Arbitrator's allocation. The proposal recognizes the contributions of all three partners and provides a workable basis to move forward together.
